Delta Secondary School, Warri, stamped its authority on the 8th Government College Ughelli Relays, winning the overall male and female titles at the inter-collegiate athletics competition in Ughelli, Delta State. Beyond their dominance on the track, the Warri-based school had another reason to celebrate as one of its athletes, Theophilus Beauty, secured a scholarship through university education, alongside financial and training support to advance her athletics career. Beauty was named Victrix Ludorum, while her schoolmate, Abruthe Ogenevwegba, claimed the Victor Ludorum award, giving Delta Secondary School a clean sweep of the competition’s two major individual honours. The scholarship was announced by Chief Andrew Oru, who pledged to sponsor Beauty’s education through university level in Nigeria. His intervention goes beyond academic sponsorship, with a commitment to provide the coaching and training resources needed to nurture her sporting ability. The school contingent equally benefited from immediate cash rewards following its impressive outing. In the relay events, Idia College, Benin City, demonstrated its strength in the women’s category, winning gold in both the 4x100m and 4x400m races. Novena University Staff School took the men’s 4x400m title. Traditional rulers HRM Uche Irenuwa, the Obi of Abavo, and HRM Albert Akpomudje, SAN, the Owhorode of Olomu Kingdom, joined Chief Oru in presenting awards to the outstanding participants. However, while the performances provided plenty of reasons for celebration, the state of the competition venue emerged as a major concern, with the athletics tracks now requiring urgent attention. Akpomudje, in his closing remarks, acknowledged the difficulties faced by the organisers and praised committee chairman Ejiro Omonode for ensuring the successful staging of the competition despite the deteriorating condition of the facility. He subsequently announced plans to establish a body that would drive the comprehensive reconstruction of the 10-year-old tartan tracks. Shell Petroleum Development Company originally constructed and donated the facility to Government College Ughelli, providing the platform for the inaugural GCU Relays in 2018. “We acknowledge Shell’s contribution to the development of the facility which heralded the first edition in 2018, but for now and moving forward the track now requires rehabilitation or replacement after years of consistent use,” Akpomudje said. The proposed reconstruction is expected to give the competition a much-needed facelift and restore the facility to a standard capable of supporting the development of young athletics talents. Organised by the Government College Ughelli Old Boys Association the annual GCU Relays was established to bring secondary school athletics back into focus, discover future stars and create a platform for young athletes to compete and develop. The event continues to enjoy backing from the GAMSU Foundation and the school’s old boys, whose support has helped sustain the competition as an important fixture on the secondary school athletics calendar.
